To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a high efficiency of deflection of high energy negative particles by a bent crystal is achieved due to a combination of the effects of doughnut scattering of high-energy particles and their recapture into bound atomic states.

the deflection efficiency of high-energy negative beam particles is high enough for practical applications, and the deflection is mainly due to scattering of particles with the atomic strings of bent crystal.
a high-efficiency deflection (90%) of a high-energy negative beam was observed in a bent crystal with the bend angle of 43 μrad.

the development of a new method for efficient high-energy particle beam deflection, which may be useful in high-energy physics, astrophysics, and accelerator physics.
the development and implementation of new methods of beam manipulation in high-energy physics.
the development of high-efficiency deflection methods for high-energy charged particle beams in a crystal.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the deflection of high energy particles by bent crystal is due to the combination of both mechanisms.
a high deflection efficiency of the beam was achieved due to a high density of atomic strings in the bent crystal.
the axial channeling in the bent silicon crystals is a very promising method of high efficiency particle deflection.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the deflection efficiency is limited by the probability of particle recapturing.
the efficiency of deflection of high energy particles through axial channel is very high.

the efficiency of deflection by axial channeling in bent crystals is much higher than that for axial channeling in flat crystals, which is of great importance for the development of high-energy particle collimation systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the deflection of high energy negative particles by bent crystals is possible with high efficiency and with a high peak-to-valley ratio.
axial channeling can be a very effective way for deflecting high-energy particles in the future high-intensity hadron colliders.
the efficiency of the deflection is high enough to make it possible to use bent crystals for high-energy negative particles.
